target_customer: Developers and startups needing background jobs, cron and delayed tasks without running queues
problem: Running reliable background task queues and cron jobs on serverless platforms is hard and distracting for small teams.
product_category: Task scheduling API and developer infrastructure

founders.name: James Martinez
founders.background_notes: YC page lists no background; Resend's announcement says he started Mergent through YC S21.

exit.reason: Resend said the team joined to improve uptime, scalability and developer experience; the Mergent blog gave no financial rationale. Service ended July 28, 2025.

competitors.name: Quirrel
competitors.what: Open source job queue and cron service for serverless platforms

technical_complexity.rationale: A reliable distributed scheduler with retries needs careful engineering, but a single founder built it on standard queue technology.

defensibility.rationale: Open source and hosted rivals offered the same scheduling; users could migrate easily, as Inngest and Trigger.dev later published migration guides.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Platforms added native cron and scheduling, and Quirrel was acquired by Netlify; Mergent itself was acquired by Resend in April 2025 and shut down in July 2025.

market_need_then: Serverless platforms lacked native queues and cron, which Quirrel's maintainer described as the reason it existed, indicating demand.

branding.domain_note: Used mergent.co; now redirects to its blog post announcing the Resend acquisition.

identity.voice_and_tone: Developer-focused: Incredibly reliable background task queues and cron jobs

branding.community_and_virality: Resend said Mergent was the first scheduler its own team used.

brand_strength.rationale: Known in a developer niche, but no press about the brand itself was found.

outcome_analysis: Mergent was a one person scheduling API that processed hundreds of billions of tasks per Resend and was acquired by Resend in April 2025 with the product sunset on July 28, 2025. No funding was found, so it was likely small. The team absorption plus product shutdown fits a soft landing rather than a venture outcome, though terms were not disclosed.
notes: The directory status says Active but the company was acquired and the service closed in July 2025. The Resend blog fetch was rate-limited, so Resend details (April 23, 2025 date, 370 billion tasks, founder name) come from a search summary of that page. The Mergent blog gives no announcement date. Quirrel's repo creation date is October 2021, a few months after the S21 batch. Acquihire label is an inference since Resend gave no terms. No funding news found.
